blocks.content: Motion is one of the most fundamental concepts in physics. A body is said to be in motion when its position changes with respect to time and a reference point. The study of motion is called mechanics, and the branch dealing only with motion without considering forces is known as kinematics.
1. Meaning of Motion

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Distance is the total length of the path traveled by an object, while displacement is the shortest distance between initial and final positions.
Speed is a scalar quantity measuring distance over time, whereas velocity is a vector quantity indicating speed with direction.
Acceleration represents the rate of change of velocity over time, measured in m/s².
Uniformly accelerated motion is described by three standard equations: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as.
On motion graphs, the slope of distance-time gives speed, while the area under a velocity-time graph gives total displacement.

blocks.content: • A body is said to be in motion if its position changes with time.
• If the position of a body does not change with time, it is said to be at rest.
• Motion is always described with respect to a reference point.

blocks.content: 4. Speed and Velocity
5. Types of Speed
Motion is the change in position of an object with respect to time and its surrounding reference frame.
• Uniform Speed – When an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
• Non-uniform Speed – When an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time.
• Average Speed – Total distance divided by total time.
6. Acceleration
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
• It can occur due to change in speed or direction.
• If velocity decreases, the acceleration is called retardation.

blocks.content: 7. Equations of Motion
For uniformly accelerated motion:
• v = u + at
• s = ut + ½ at²
• v² = u² + 2as
8. Graphs of Motion
• Distance–Time Graph shows how distance changes with time.
• Velocity–Time Graph shows how velocity changes with time.
• Slope of distance-time graph gives speed.

items: Displacement can be zero, positive, or negative, but distance covered by a moving object is always strictly positive.
The area under a Velocity-Time graph represents total displacement, while its slope gives acceleration.
When an object completes a circular path of radius 'r', its distance is 2πr but its net displacement is zero.

blocks.content: • Area under velocity-time graph gives displacement.
Important Facts
• Motion is defined as change in position with time.
• Speed is a scalar quantity while velocity is a vector quantity.
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
• Equations of motion are valid only for uniform acceleration.
